title: Semisimple rational points of group schemes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. A rational point $s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ (using the affine spectrum convention of [def-sc-gm-ga]) is semisimple if for every finite-dimensional algebraic representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ [def-wf-algebraic-representations], the linear automorphism $\rho_k(s)$ is diagonalizable over $k$. Equivalently, for every finite index set $I$, and every homomorphism of group schemes $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(k^I)$, there exist $P\in\operatorname{GL}_I(k)$ and $(d_i)_{i\in I}\in k^I$ such that $P^{-1}\rho_k(s)P=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)$. The empty index set is included.
